text:
sam_support: acme reports Private control plane mTLS failures after an egress firewall push. ~1k failed handshakes from their NAT over the last hour, app errors and 503s. anyone seen this pattern?

ops-bot: ALERT: control-plane observed 1189 TLS handshake resets from 3.45.67.89 between 2026-03-16T14:20:05Z and 2026-03-16T14:30:02Z

neha_sre: can you attach a pcap and openssl s_client output from a bastion? need the ClientHello + server behavior.

acme_netops: attaching brief s_client and a link to pcap: https://files.acme/example-mtls.pcap (first 200 packets). s_client:

```
$ openssl s_client -connect cp-1.private.redwood.ai:443 -key client.key -cert client.crt -servername cp-1.private.redwood.ai -alpn h2
CONNECTED(00000003)
139678234: SSL routines:tls_process_client_hello:no shared cipher
---
no peer certificate available
---
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 232 bytes
```

kevin_oncall: two quick suspects: 1) TLS inspection or corporate NGFW trimming or rewriting ClientHello (SNI/ALPN/keyshare). 2) MTU/fragmentation causing ClientHello fragmentation and proxy resetting. do we see TCP RSTs from an inline proxy?

neha_sre: also confirm their edge is allowing outbound IPs, not only FQDN. some proxies allow domain but block direct IPs or vice versa. ask them to `curl --resolve` to force the control-plane IP and see if behavior changes.

acme_netops: tried --resolve -> still fails. pcap shows TLS ClientHello split across two TCP segments; our inline proxy (secure-inspect) is doing ssl-bump and is inserting its own cert and not forwarding client cert chain. looks like client cert never reached Redwood.

kevin_oncall: that explains mTLS failure. many SSL proxies terminate TLS and do not forward raw client certs to upstream. for mTLS you need TLS passthrough or a proxy that supports proxy-protocol + client cert forwarding. short-term: add control-plane FQDN to policy bypass for TLS inspection. also check ALPN and SNI passthrough because some proxies strip or truncate SNI.

eng-platform: I will pull control-plane logs for 3.45.67.89 around 1766543205 and look for TLS reason codes. if we see 'client cert missing' or 'no shared cipher' we'll confirm proxy termination.

neha_sre: please give them repro steps to collect deterministic artifacts:
1) From their bastion run: `openssl s_client -connect cp-1.private.redwood.ai:443 -key client.key -cert client.crt -servername cp-1.private.redwood.ai -alpn h2 -msg -debug` and paste the output.
2) tcpdump on their edge: `sudo tcpdump -nn -s0 -w /tmp/mtls.pcap host 3.45.67.89 and port 443` then share first 200 packets.
3) test bypass: `curl --resolve cp-1.private.redwood.ai:443:3.45.67.89 -v https://cp-1.private.redwood.ai/health` – note whether TLS negotiation completes and whether we see client cert presented.

acme_netops: will run those. quick Q: is there any control-plane requirement for ALPN values? our proxy forces `http/1.1` for inspection, could that be relevant?

neha_sre: control-plane expects HTTP/2 (h2) for some routes but will accept http/1.1; the mTLS handshake itself shouldn't require h2, but keyshares/extension handling in TLS1.3 might be broken by some proxies. if proxy mutates keyshare or truncates extensions the server may abort with no shared cipher / handshake failure.

kevin_oncall: pragmatic mitigation: if they can't disable inspection, they can add NAT egress IPs to our allowlist and mark as TLS passthrough on their proxy. I can enable a temporary ingress rule for those NATs to reduce RSTs while they change proxy policy. will need approval from eng-platform for short-lived exception.

eng-platform: approved for a 48h temporary passthrough window for NAT 3.45.67.88-3.45.67.90. I logged an internal ticket (ENG-PLAT-7642) to correlate logs and follow up with a permanent doc change.

sam_support: thanks — asking customer to try bypass and send outputs. escalating to eng-platform for log correlation and to docs for an 'mTLS behind TLS-inspection' troubleshooting note. :thumbsup:

acme_netops: confirmed bypass worked when we routed directly (no proxy): TLS handshake completed and health returns 200. we'll roll out a policy change and report back. thanks for the fast triage.

sam_support: closing loop when they confirm prod fix. if they hit further errors ping here and we'll reopen.
